what_happened: The job "Run independent plan-group items in parallel in the drain loop" ended failed at admission, before any work was done. Admission refused the change because athena.toml no longer parses. The file has a new `[parallel]` table at line 166, and the config schema does not know a `parallel` field. It accepts only athena, models, budget, agents, capabilities, classes, forecast, secrets, tools, history, records, personal_data and landing. No acceptance criteria, blocker or major findings, or failed checks are listed. Nothing was delivered.
cause: The config file and the code that parses it are changed separately, and nothing checks that a new config section is known to the parser. The new `[parallel]` table was added to athena.toml (by the job's plan or by hand) without a matching schema field, and the parser rejects unknown fields. Neither planning nor the request reading checks that an edit to a protected config file parses under the schema that will exist at admission. The error therefore surfaces only when admission refuses the job, so no work is attempted.
prevention: Run a parse check of athena.toml against the schema as part of the edit and before admission. It should run when a config change is planned, and again on the job's resulting diff. A job whose outcome needs a new config section must deliver the schema field, its default and the section together, with a test that loads an athena.toml containing it. Admission should also report the offending section as a missing schema deliverable, not only as a parse error.
proposed_request: Make athena run independent plan-group items in parallel in the drain loop. Outcome: when a plan group has items that do not depend on each other, the drain runs them at the same time, up to a configurable limit, and one item's failure does not stop the others. Default behavior with no config stays as it is now (one item at a time). Configuration: add a `parallel` section to the athena.toml schema, with a maximum-concurrency setting that defaults to 1, and add it to athena.toml only together with the schema field, so that athena.toml parses at every commit. Acceptance: (1) a test loads an athena.toml that contains the `[parallel]` section and passes; (2) a test with a limit of 1 shows items run strictly in order as before; (3) a test with a limit above 1 shows two independent items running at the same time, and a dependent item waiting for what it depends on; (4) ordering and retry rules are unchanged; (5) `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check` pass, and the final report maps each criterion to its evidence.
